title: Antarctica's Bleeding Glacier
sources: Mikucki & Priscu 2007 (PMC1932727): marine-origin brine hosting microbes on reduced iron/sulfur
Zoumplis et al. 2026, Nature Geoscience: marine-derived microbial signatures at the terminus
Taylor 1911 red-algae guess (Scientific American, Mental Floss)
hedge_notes: No firm age exists - never say 'millions of years'
'Scientists think' is required on the ocean-origin line
Do not claim 'no oxygen' - not confirmed in sources checked

segments.label: BLOOD FALLS
segments.text: In Antarctica, a glacier is bleeding.
segments.prompt: a blood red stream flowing down a glacier in Antarctica

segments.label: RED STREAM
segments.text: A blood-red stream pours from Taylor Glacier onto the ice below.
segments.prompt: red stained ice below a glacier wall

segments.text: In 1911, the explorer who found it blamed red algae.
segments.prompt: an early 1900s polar expedition on the ice

segments.label: IRON RUSTS
segments.text: It was not algae. It is salty water, rich in iron. When the iron hits the air, it rusts.
segments.prompt: rusty red water over white ice

segments.label: TRAPPED BRINE
segments.text: That water comes from a brine trapped under the glacier. Scientists think it is ocean water, sealed away when the sea retreated.
segments.prompt: a frozen lake in Antarctica surrounded by ice cliffs

segments.label: LIFE WITHOUT SUN
segments.text: Down there, there is no sunlight. Yet microbes live on, using the chemistry of iron and sulfur.
segments.prompt: microscopic bacteria glowing under a microscope

segments.label: CLUES
segments.text: Scientists study it for clues about life in extreme places.
segments.prompt: a lone researcher on the Antarctic ice

segments.label: UNDER THE ICE
segments.text: What else is hiding under the ice?
